body.x: ROBOBLOCK System (CEO Dae-Seob Shin, www.roboblock.co.kr) introduced its 3D printer and educational robot system at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

Its 3D printer "New X-More" is capable of rendering 3-dimensional products into images for print and is especially effective and easy to use in product research or sample production. It can be used in small spaces and can print using both PLA and ABS printing materials. Printing can be done once the image is converted into an STL file and the software to do so is included with the 3D printer.

The ROBOBLOCK Kit comes with an assembly of plastic block frames which can be freely connected to make robots and blocks. The different shaped and sized blocks can be used to assemble different forms while the motor box allows changes in the gear ratio to control its speed at three different levels. The DC motor uses AA batteries to operate and the kits come with a robot manual for programming.

The kits were designed for novice robot builders as well as to develop the intelligence and creativity of children. They are in use at a number of schools and educational facilities and have been lauded for its ability to produce more than 15 different kinds of robots.

“Through the upcoming CES 2015, we plan to introduce our high quality 3D printers to the American market--the base of 3D printing,” said a spokesperson for ROBOBLOCK System. “In addition to the American-based Robotshop, we plan to meet with a number of potential buyers to expand exports of our ROBOBLOCK kits.”

ROBOBLOCK System began in 2000 and includes a variety of items in its products portfolio including 3D printers, educational robots, toy robots, robot controllers, motors, micro controllers, block robots, and more.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
